### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/knowledge-ragflow`, `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-knowledge/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class), KnowledgeServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via admitSources (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService), applyPermissionFilter (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService), getReadableFields (symbol, a method of interface KnowledgeFieldSecurity), isSystemObjectName (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class), KnowledgeServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), getQueryableFields (symbol, a method of interface KnowledgeFieldSecurity), getReadableFields (symbol, a method of interface KnowledgeFieldSecurity))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx`  _(via /object/:name/state/:field (route, bridged from symbol isObjectPackageDisabled — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via applyPermissionFilter (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via getLegalNextStates (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getLegalNextStates, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name/state/:field; the bare tail of client method meta.getLegalNextStates, bound to GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field), meta.getLegalNextStates (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name/state/:field, selected by route anchor /object/:name/state/:field; the route ledger binds it to GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field, selected by route anchor /object/:name/state/:field))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-2.mdx`  _(via getLegalNextStates (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getLegalNextStates, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name/state/:field; the bare tail of client method meta.getLegalNextStates, bound to GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field), meta.getLegalNextStates (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name/state/:field, selected by route anchor /object/:name/state/:field; the route ledger binds it to GET /meta/object/:name/state/:field, selected by route anchor /object/:name/state/:field))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via getQueryableFields (symbol, a method of interface KnowledgeFieldSecurity), getReadableFields (symbol, a method of interface KnowledgeFieldSecurity))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-knowledge/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8f141a28dc6f179ad10dfe018e0cf0c93346d0c3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d7316f8d11fe31e4930d8b8850f9f25486a427ea` — the merge of head `2c9abeffeb0e5b88fd6a3087743d41dbf28a0f32` into base `8f141a28dc6f179ad10dfe018e0cf0c93346d0c3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d7316f8d11fe31e4930d8b8850f9f25486a427ea && git checkout d7316f8d11fe31e4930d8b8850f9f25486a427ea
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8f141a28dc6f179ad10dfe018e0cf0c93346d0c3 2c9abeffeb0e5b88fd6a3087743d41dbf28a0f32 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8f141a28dc6f179ad10dfe018e0cf0c93346d0c3 && git merge --no-ff 2c9abeffeb0e5b88fd6a3087743d41dbf28a0f32

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8f141a28dc6f179ad10dfe018e0cf0c93346d0c3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8f141a28dc6f179ad10dfe018e0cf0c93346d0c3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#4 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYpEsWWE9Y5YtSsDgqZ

## 席位核对 — L1 REWORK · head `774652cd63edbc0f93d3a113814072ac147f195e` · 2026-11-24T07:48Z

- **Shape.** Draft PR to `main`, first line `Fixes #36839` (merging closes the card; the diff delivers all of Expected 1–5, so `Fixes` is right). `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`, copied verbatim from the claim (os-dev.md:276). 10 files, all on governed-free paths (`governedPathsIn` → `[]`). `l1-face`: every line ok except one **flag, `changeset`**: `@objectstack/core` is touched with no entry. Cleared on reading: the only core file is `src/security/row-serving-door-exposure.pin.test.ts`, and core ships `files: [dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md]`, so the diff publishes nothing from core. `@objectstack/dogfood` is private. `@objectstack/service-knowledge` carries the `patch` changeset.
- **Premise and delivery against the card.** The premises hold, and the dev showed each one: `security` is resolved per search; `getQueryableFields` exists on plugin-security; `getSchema` and `registry` exist on the bound engine; and the disabled-package check needs no injected hook, because `registryObjectPackageDisabled` comes from `@objectstack/core`, which the package already depends on.
  - E1: the PR drops a source whose object is in a disabled package, fails `canServeApiOperation(enable,'search')`, or is a `sys_*` object without `isAiReadExposed`. It drops the source before the search, which is stronger than dropping the hit after it. The system context still bypasses.
  - E2: the field gate covers `contentFields` (`'*'` meaning every declared field), `metadataFields` and `title`, less the credential and `internal` fields. It checks them against `getQueryableFields`, falling back to `getReadableFields` minus `maskingRule` fields, and to the `maskingRule` rule alone when no service is registered. Adding `metadataFields` is a justified widening, and the PR body states it.
  - E3: no spec key is added, and the narrowing is stated in the changeset and in knowledge.mdx §5, §7.1 and §9.
  - E4: the pin now holds the door by name in `HELD_BY_NAME`, and the matrix note is updated.
  - E5: there are 16 pins through the real `KnowledgeService`, 2 of them through `KnowledgeServicePlugin` on a real `LiteKernel`. They include a caller who can read the row but not the field, and an object with `apiEnabled:false`.
  - Push-down (PD5): admission runs once per (caller, object) per search, as one `getSchema` call, one registry probe and one field answer. No query runs per hit, and no ids are materialised. The row re-check is unchanged (one `$in` query per object).
- **Gates.** Check-runs on `774652cd63`: 60 success, 10 skipped (all expected opt-in or queue-only), 0 failed, 0 pending. Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are both success.
- **Test evidence.** The dev gives a red-before/green-after reading: with `knowledge-service.ts` and the plugin restored to base `f77d078d` (blob match), the new file fails 14 and passes 2, and the 2 that pass are the pure preservation tests. At HEAD it passes 16/16. The pin's new by-name test is red at base (1 failed, 3 passed) and green at HEAD (4/4). The commands are named and the counts reported, but no raw output is pasted, which is acceptable here. The refusals return empty results rather than an error envelope, so there is no `code`/`status` for the tests to assert.
- **Sentence reads.** I read three texts sentence by sentence against the code.
  - The changeset: every bullet matches `knowledge-source-admission.ts` except one sentence (finding M1).
  - knowledge.mdx: §5 diagram, the new "Source admission" subsection, §7.1 and §9 all match, with M1 and N2 as the exceptions. "granting `list` does" is held by a test.
  - system-context.mdx: row 46 and the register row `admitSources | 1 | 46` match.
  - The matrix note matches.
  - content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx:76 (flagged by the drift check) describes only RLS. It is still true, just incomplete (N5).
- **Findings.**
  - **must-fix M1**: `knowledge-service-plugin.ts:126-132` swallows every throw from `ctx.getService('security')` and treats it as "no security service". That falls back to the `maskingRule`-only rule, which admits a source whose hidden field is hidden only by a permission-set rule. On the in-repo kernels a missing service is reported as a throw, so this code cannot tell an absent service from a registered service that cannot be used (for example, a factory registration, which throws "is async"). The analytics door documents the opposite stance: a throw is UNUSABLE and refuses (`service-analytics/src/plugin.ts:~683-740`). Meanwhile `.changeset/36839-knowledge-exposure-fls.md:17` and `knowledge.mdx:322` both say "Every gate fails closed: a lookup that throws … keeps the source out", which is false for this lookup. The fix is one of these:
    - (preferred) read absence from the registry, and let any other throw propagate into `admitObject`, which already fails closed. Add one test for this.
    - Or narrow both sentences to say what the code does.

    `mcp/src/plugin.ts:515-521` uses the same swallow, which is why this is a one-round fix and not a redesign.
  - **nit N1**: `row-serving-door-exposure.pin.test.ts:37-39,153` describes "the MCP door's `search_knowledge`" and "the `search_knowledge` tool every door builds on it". At this head, no in-repo code serves that tool (only the name constant exists in spec). The sentence becomes true once #36823 lands, which timing 甲 puts after this PR.
  - **nit N2**: `knowledge.mdx:309` says "`'*'` meaning every field the object declares", but the code leaves out `id`. Harmless.
  - **nit N3**: `knowledge-service.ts:378` awaits each object's admission in turn. Running them in parallel would cut latency; there is no correctness effect.
  - **nit N4 (seat)**: the claim's file surface (comment 7121224645, never edited) does not list `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`. The census gate required that file, and the PR body names it. Record this in the ACCEPT.
  - **nit N5**: content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx:76 could point to the §5 narrowing. Optional.
- **L2 face.** `record-recognisers --template --paths <10 files>`: the paths alone decide no face, so the changeset's `Clause-②: no` line (with no arm) decides. Scope has no hits, no governed path is touched, and **no L2 is owed** at the declared line. One decision is left to the seat: execution-duties.md:106/108 says a runtime security-behaviour change is not clause ②, and only a narrowed published accept set takes the arm. But recent security narrowings #36386 and #36518 declared `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with a `!` title. If the seat revises the claim to `(narrowing)`, these all become owed:
  - the `!` title,
  - the dogfood battery,
  - a `Skills-docs:` line,
  - an L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` over the whole non-prose diff.
- **Disclosure.** The PR body, changeset and commits name the class (missing FLS and exposure enforcement on a row-serving door), the location and the functions. None of them gives a request body or step-by-step reproduction. Clean.
- **Out of scope.** None filed. `declaredFields` accepts both the array and the record form of `fields`, the same as analytics' `maskingRuleFields`. I am not raising it.

### Adversarial review (read-only, effort xhigh, on this head) — findings folded into this round

- **M1 above = its hole 1** (any throw from the `security` lookup read as "no security service"; the analytics door refuses instead).
- **S2 (should-fix)** — `packages/plugins/knowledge-ragflow/src/index.ts` ~153/161/180 searches a whole dataset and stamps every hit with the searched source's id, ignoring the stored `objectstack_source_id`; `KnowledgeService.search` never checks a hit's origin. Two sources sharing a dataset ⇒ a search of an admitted source can return chunks of a refused one. Fix: filter or verify on the stored source id and drop hits whose source is not the searched one; pin it.
- **S3 (should-fix)** — `knowledge-service.ts` ~343/352: the no-context / no-engine path skips admission on the premise that `applyPermissionFilter` drops every object-source hit, but ~479 keeps any hit without a `sourceRecordId` before checking the source kind. Fix: in those two cases drop object sources inside `admitSources`; pin it.
- Nits (no push for these alone): `sys_*` check reads the raw object string, not the resolved schema name (`knowledge-source-admission.ts` ~172); `'*'` drift between indexing (every string key) and the gate (declared fields) (`servedFieldsOf` ~212 vs `recordToDocument` ~548).

### Seat decisions on this round

- **Clause-②:** stays `no` without a `(narrowing)` arm — execution-duties.md: a runtime permission/security behaviour change is not clause ②; what narrows here is what a restricted caller is served, not a published accept set.
- **N4:** `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` was required by a repo gate and is named in the PR body — accepted as a surface addition.
